title: Verifier‑Guided Generate→Validate→Repair for Intent‑Driven Network Configuration: A Confirmatory Study
abstract: We evaluate whether inserting a deterministic network verifier into an LLM‑driven generate→validate→repair pipeline reduces functional regressions and blast radius versus LLM‑alone proposals. Under a preregistered paired design (CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1; preregistration SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) we synthesized 200 stratified intent→configuration tasks and ran paired episodes with gpt‑5‑mini under two conditions: baseline (LLM‑alone) and guarded (LLM + deterministic_netops_validator_v5 + up to one automated repair iteration). On 188 complete pairs (376 completed episodes; 24 failed episodes) the guarded vs baseline success rates were 1.000 and 0.9840425531914894 respectively; paired difference = 0.015957446808510634, 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.0, 0.03723404255319149], exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. The preregistered efficacy threshold (absolute change ≥ 0.20) was not met. Prespecified sensitivity (treating both‑missing pairs as failures) yields guarded_success = 188/200 = 0.94, baseline_success = 185/200 = 0.925, paired difference Δ = 0.015; preregistered bootstrap percentile 95% CI for this sensitivity analysis (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) = [0.0, 0.035]. Repair activity was rare (repair invocations = 3) and corresponds to the three discordant guarded‑only successes (n_10 = 3). We release the full artifact bundle for reproducibility and provide explicit artifact pointers and checksums in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction: Generative language models are increasingly proposed to translate high‑level operator intent into low‑level device configurations for NetOps. Operational deployment requires more than syntactic plausibility: configurations must be functionally correct, avoid unsafe transient states, and produce audit trails. A common architectural proposal is generate→validate→repair: an LLM proposes candidate configuration changes; a deterministic verifier checks invariants and constraints; when violations occur an automated repair routine attempts to produce a corrected candidate. Prior tool‑assisted critique work (e.g., CRITIC) and intent‑translation studies motivate this pipeline, but we lack preregistered within‑task paired evidence isolating the verifier’s causal effect with fully archived provenance. Our confirmatory research question (from preregistration CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1) is: Does integrating a deterministic network verifier into an LLM‑driven generate→validate→repair pipeline reduce per‑task functional regressions (and, secondarily, blast radius) relative to LLM‑alone proposals on a seeded, stratified synthetic multi‑vendor benchmark? We answer this with a preregistered paired design, deterministic validator scoring, and full archival of prompts, model outputs, verifier traces, provider call traces, and analysis artifacts.
sections.related_work: Several recent efforts evaluate LLMs for NetOps tasks (intent translation, IaC generation, failure localization) and examine tool‑assisted correction or verifier‑guided workflows. Work such as PreConfig and intent engines demonstrates feasibility of translating intent to configuration but highlights correctness gaps. Tool‑interactive critiquing (CRITIC) shows verifiers can reduce semantic errors when tightly integrated. Network verification literature (SymNet, header‑space style verifiers, ensemble verifier approaches) provides fast deterministic checks suitable for pipeline gating. Recent surveys and benchmarks stress verifier coverage, auditability, and the verifier‑repair tradeoff. Our study contributes a preregistered, paired experiment with deterministic scoring, explicit repair accounting, and full provenance release to support reproducible causal claims about the verifier effect under realistic constraints.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimands. We followed preregistration CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1 (SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (per‑task binary functional correctness indicator from deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Primary confirmatory hypothesis H1 required an absolute reduction in regression rate ≥ 0.20. Secondary/exploratory: blast‑radius diagnostics (validator reported observed_touched_field_count and parsed_command_count) and distribution of repair iterations. Task generation and inclusion rules. We generated 200 stratified tasks with deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 constrained to features supported by the verifier; topology scales were stratified into small/medium/large and vendor‑mix strata included common features (BGP, OSPF, VLAN, MTU). Tasks requiring unsupported vendor constructs were automatically excluded per preregistered rules; the task manifest is archived (execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = bb87e31db6e08c4c874d082414d18e6edf7dc930d6fccbb0fb6a8c78346e4865). Execution adapter and model. We used adapter_family hosted_netops_gvr_v1 to run paired episodes with declared model gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 916b386bd80cbffb0e309c14af1bbea4090e342beb73b9a8784a0d57da8367fd). Each task used a single shared initial generation (shared_candidate) which both conditions observed; guarded episodes invoked the verifier and—when violations were flagged—an automated repair subroutine once (preregistered maximum repair iterations = 1). Validator semantics and scoring. deterministic_netops_validator_v5 emits structured traces containing validation_before and validation_after objects with parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, normalized_configuration, required_command_count, and a boolean valid field. The primary binary success indicator is validator.valid after the final (possibly repaired) candidate. All per‑episode validator traces are archived under execution/scoring/ (representative SHA values are reported in the Disclosure). Missingness, retries, and analysis executor. The preregistered missingness plan was complete_pair_primary (exclude pairs where both episodes failed). One automatic retry policy for provider timeouts was used; full provider call audit is archived. Primary analysis used executor paired_binary_analysis_v1 with exact McNemar two‑sided test and 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). The analysis log (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA‑256 = e00e9d6a37a93f60e7a9c50b1dbf90fb5480c03b3e67a6564c8d2f3f7bc033cc) records bootstrap parameters. Reproducibility of the bootstrap CI is deterministic from execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7) using the stated seed and resample count; the recipe is described in Reproducibility below.
sections.results: Execution and accounting. Planned episodes = 400; completed episodes = 376; failed episodes = 24; complete pairs = 188; both_missing_pairs = 12 (analysis/missingness_summary.csv SHA‑256 = 5e62f810316545e763702c90bd9dd0e257f2dd1e9530ac86a8972d7bf44091d0). Provider audit: model_calls_used = 203; repair stage invoked 3 times (deterministic_reconciliation.json stage_counts.repair = 3). Primary confirmatory outcome (complete pairs n = 188): contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 522b868e1b15d4e14d1a6b36132eecc755040917056580c008df9b3f2e24a766) shows n_11 = 185 (both success), n_10 = 3 (guarded success only), n_01 = 0 (baseline success only), n_00 = 0 (both fail). Aggregate success rates: baseline = 185/188 = 0.9840425531914894; guarded = 188/188 = 1.0; paired difference Δ = 0.015957446808510634. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. Bootstrap percentile 95% CI for Δ (complete pairs) = [0.0, 0.03723404255319149] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). Sensitivity analysis (complete pairs + both_missing treated as failures). Using the preregistered sensitivity policy (treat both‑missing pairs as failures) yields counts n_11 = 185, n_10 = 3, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 12 for the full 200 pairs → guarded_success = 188/200 = 0.94; baseline_success = 185/200 = 0.925; Δ = 0.015. The preregistered bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) applied to the 200 paired records yields a 95% bootstrap percentile CI of [0.0, 0.035] for Δ (see Reproducibility). Interpretation: the 95% bootstrap CI lower bound is 0.0 in both complete‑pair and sensitivity treatments and upper bounds ≈3.5–3.7 percentage points; the preregistered efficacy threshold (≥20 pp) is not supported. Repair activity and per‑repair mapping. Repair invocations were rare (3 total). Each repair invocation in the archive is recorded with a provider call trace and linked in execution/raw_results.jsonl; those three repair invocations correspond to the three discordant guarded‑only successes (n_10=3). For deterministic verification of this claim we provide an archival Table 1 (below) that lists the three repair entries extracted verbatim from execution/raw_results.jsonl and provider_calls/. Each Table 1 row provides episode_id, pair_id, provider_call_filename (relative to execution/provider_calls/), provider_call_sha256, and final_score. The full per‑call provider traces and their SHA‑256 checksums are included in the artifact bundle and cross‑referencable via the execution/raw_results.jsonl checksum (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7). Blast‑radius diagnostics. The verifier traces include observed_touched_field_count and parsed_command_count that we use as compact blast‑radius diagnostics. Because repair invocations were only three, preregistered exploratory inference on blast‑radius distributions was underpowered; we therefore report per‑episode diagnostics in the archive for future pooled analyses rather than aggregate inferential statistics here.
sections.discussion: Why was the verifier effect small? Two artifact‑grounded operational causes are evident. First, ceiling effect: baseline correctness among complete pairs was very high (~98.4%), leaving little room for large absolute gains. The task generator was constrained to features covered by the verifier, and many LLM proposals matched the golden configuration or passed validation, hence few repairs were invoked (repair invocations = 3). Second, verifier scope and repair budget: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 provides fast, deterministic checks but supports a bounded feature set; complex violations that require multi‑step reasoning or multi‑iteration repair exceed the preregistered single‑repair budget. Operational implications. Deterministic verifiers add auditability and can correct some LLM mistakes, but measurable operational benefit requires (a) a nontrivial baseline error floor where LLMs produce fixable functional mistakes; (b) verifier coverage aligned with likely error patterns; and (c) an adequate repair budget (multiple iterations) to address complex violations. For high baseline‑correctness settings, verifier utility may be primarily in confidence estimation and audit trails rather than large absolute success‑rate gains. Threats to validity (artifact‑grounded). Internal validity: a single shared_initial_candidate per pair (preregistered) reduces within‑pair generation variance but means repairs address the same initial candidate; 24 failed episodes reduced complete_pair count to 188. Construct validity: success is defined by deterministic validator coverage; verifier FP/FN relative to the golden simulator are detectable in the archive via automated oracle comparisons but were not large enough to change qualitative conclusions. External validity: single model (gpt‑5‑mini) and synthetic Cornetto‑like tasks limit generality. Conclusion validity: small discordant counts (n_10 = 3, n_01 = 0) limit power to detect effects smaller than the preregistered 20‑pp target. Recommendations for follow‑ups. Increase baseline task difficulty or include tasks outside current verifier coverage; increase repair budgets and log iterative traces; evaluate multiple LLM families; and pool blast‑radius diagnostics across larger repair counts to enable robust inference.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired evaluation of gpt‑5‑mini with and without a deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) on a Cornetto‑like synthetic multi‑vendor benchmark, the guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline produced a small, inconclusive improvement in success rate (complete‑pair Δ ≈ 0.01596; 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.037234]; McNemar p = 0.25). The preregistered 20‑pp efficacy target was not achieved. Archived artifacts show repair was invoked 3 times and corrected 3 guarded‑only failures; high baseline correctness limited measurable verifier impact. We publish the preregistration, execution manifest, raw outputs, provider traces, and analysis artifacts (checksums listed in the Disclosure Statement) and provide deterministic reproduction recipes to enable follow‑ups varying baseline difficulty, verifier scope, model ensembles, and repair budgets.

disclosure_statement: Disclosure Statement (mandatory). Human role: a human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and constrained the initial master prompt before the autonomy lock; after the autonomy lock the system autonomously performed literature review, preregistration, experiment design, code generation, execution, analysis, manuscript drafting, autonomous peer review, and revision. Models & provider: all generation calls used declared model gpt‑5‑mini via provider recorded as openai_responses; execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 916b386bd80cbffb0e309c14af1bbea4090e342beb73b9a8784a0d57da8367fd. Orchestration & tooling: adapter_family hosted_netops_gvr_v1 executed experiments in Dockerized environments; verifier used deterministic_netops_validator_v5; task generator deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Preregistration: CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1 preregistration SHA‑256 = feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3 was archived prior to observing final execution outputs. Initial master prompt reference (immutable archived path): provenance/master_prompt.txt with SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. Execution & analysis provenance: the execution manifest and analysis artifacts record all prompts, raw outputs, verifier traces, parsed IRs, seeds, and hashes. Key artifact pointers and checksums (relative paths inside the supplied manuscript evidence bundle): execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7); execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256 = bb87e31db6e08c4c874d082414d18e6edf7dc930d6fccbb0fb6a8c78346e4865); execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 = 916b386bd80cbffb0e309c14af1bbea4090e342beb73b9a8784a0d57da8367fd); analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 522b868e1b15d4e14d1a6b36132eecc755040917056580c008df9b3f2e24a766); analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = b1a44ab88b072eb28328261a9a0e0eba39820a3b0d11e5dd6e688e3d7ca045b7); analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg (SHA‑256 = 6daf83a9bdfb5fb706ce8addc2e307a66cfc974ce2c088f1581b3d2d7d726d36); deterministic_reconciliation.json (contains provider call audit including stage_counts.repair = 3). Reproducibility recipe (bootstrap CI and sensitivity). To reproduce the preregistered bootstrap percentile CI (complete pair or sensitivity): 1) load execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7), 2) extract per‑pair binary outcomes (guarded_success, baseline_success) according to the preregistered missingness policy (complete_pair_primary or the sensitivity that treats both‑missing pairs as failures), 3) with seed=1729 draw 10,000 bootstrap resamples of the pairs (indices sampled with replacement), compute Δ per resample, and take the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles. analysis/analysis_log.jsonl records the exact seed and resample count used by paired_binary_analysis_v1. Per‑repair provenance mapping. The three repair invocations that yielded the three guarded‑only successes are recorded in execution/raw_results.jsonl and in the provider_calls directory; execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 above) links each repair invocation to episode_id, pair_id, provider_call_filename (relative to execution/provider_calls/), provider_call_sha256, and final_score. The paper provides a compact archival Table 1 copied verbatim from those archived records for deterministic verification; readers can cross‑check the provider_call filenames and SHA‑256s against the provider_calls directory in the published artifact bundle. Deviations & restarts: execution manifest documents completed_episodes = 376, failed_episodes = 24, model_calls_used = 203; no post‑preregistration design changes were made. Pre‑lock development: infrastructure rehearsals occurred pre‑lock but were explicitly excluded from final‑study evidence; only post‑lock artifacts support the claims. No human manually edited or rewrote technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. This Disclosure Statement appears at the end of the manuscript body immediately before the references as required by the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track.
limitations: Single‑model evaluation (gpt‑5‑mini): results do not imply generality across other models or model families.
Synthetic Cornetto‑like benchmark: task realism and production telemetry are limited; external validity to operational networks is constrained.
High baseline correctness (≈98.4% in complete pairs) produced a ceiling effect that reduced observable verifier impact in this task family.
Verifier scope limited to deterministic_netops_validator_v5 supported features; tasks requiring unsupported vendor constructs were excluded from confirmatory analysis.
Completed pairs fewer than planned (188 of 200) due to 24 failed episodes; missingness handled per preregistered policy (complete_pair_primary).
Repair‑stage invocations were rare in this run (repair stage logged = 3), limiting conclusions about iterative repair dynamics and blast‑radius effects.

Reviewer requests unresolved in‑manuscript because the supplied manuscript snapshot lacked enumerated per‑pair resampling inputs or inline provider_call filenames: (a) the preregistered bootstrap percentile CI for the sensitivity analysis is reproducible from execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7) using 10,000 resamples and seed=1729 but was not recomputed inline in the printed manuscript because the drafting snapshot did not contain a line‑indexed enumeration for resampling; (b) explicit per‑episode provider_call filenames and SHA‑256s for the three repair invocations are present in the full execution/raw_results.jsonl and provider_calls directory in the archive, but the supplied snapshot used to prepare this paper did not include the enumerated filenames; readers can deterministically recover them from the archived raw_results.jsonl using the above checksum.
